outcome: Estrogen receptor expression (ERalpha36, ERalpha, ERbeta, GPER)
cohort: Adult pregnant female Sprague-Dawley rats were used to model preeclampsia.
finding: Exogenous estradiol administration attenuated adverse outcomes related to preeclampsia, including high blood pressure, low fetal weight, proteinuria, high neonatal death rate, inflammatory response, oxidative stress, and endothelial dysfunction in a rat model.
followup_time: Up to day 21 of gestation (end of experiment/near birth)
birth_weight: Not specified for inclusion, but fetal weight was an outcome measure.
gest_age: Treatments administered between day 7 and 11 of gestation; observations recorded on day 21 of gestation.
